citations.narrative:
The facility self-reported an incident that occurred on July 10, 2026, involving an adult male wildebeest who was able to
escape their enclosure. At the time of the incident the animal was in the veldt exhibit in the Africa section. The facility
believes the animal was able to traverse through a pond in the enclosure, breach a barrier within the pond, and make it to
the opposite shore. The animal was then able to breach a secondary fence that is approximately 4 foot tall. Facility
employees found the animal outside the enclosure within close proximity to a path that is open to the public. The facility
evacuated the area and the animal was able to be returned to the enclosure. The incident did not result in harm to the
animal or the public. Enclosures that do not properly contain animals can result in injury and stress to the regulated
animals and the public. Correct by ensuring that the facility is constructed of materials and of such strength as appropriate
for the animals housed in the enclosure to protect them from injury and to contain the animals. Correct by 5-AUG-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with Facility Representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
